correctness|src/ui/MappingRows.tsx|962|p.title: Preserve numeric settings when changing a copy source
correctness|src/ui/MappingRows.tsx|962|p.why_it_matters: A user can configure a copied output as Number with whole-number, scale and rounding rules, then change its Copy source dropdown. The dropdown calls match(), which always sets type to text; the new update logic also removes all numeric settings. The replacement source now bypasses numeric validation and exports as text, so a fractional or malformed value that should be invalid can become eligible without an explicit change to the output type or validation controls.

src/ui/MappingRows.tsx:126-130: patch.type === "text" clears rounding, scale and wholeNumber in update().
src/ui/MappingRows.tsx:978-987: Copy outputs now expose an independent Output type selector, including Number.
src/engine/recipes.ts:196-199: Numeric validation is conditional on f.type === "number".
correctness|src/ui/MappingRows.tsx|962|p.suggested_fix: For an existing copy recipe, change only the recipe source and preserve the field's output type and numeric settings. Reserve the explicit text reset for transitions from another recipe mode when required. Add a regression scenario that configures a numeric copy with wholeNumber/scale/rounding, changes its source, and verifies those settings and invalid-row behavior remain intact.

adversarial|src/ui/MappingRows.tsx|128|c.title: Changing numeric source silently removes validation
adversarial|src/ui/MappingRows.tsx|128|c.why_it_matters: A user who changes the source of an existing numeric copy unexpectedly converts the destination to text and loses its whole-number, scale and rounding rules. Fractional or malformed quantities then become valid exportable text. The same problem occurs when selecting number output and its rules before choosing the first source.
evidence: src/ui/MappingRows.tsx:128: rounding: undefined,; src/ui/MappingRows.tsx:129: scale: undefined,; src/ui/MappingRows.tsx:130: wholeNumber: undefined,; src/ui/MappingRows.tsx:150: update(id, { type: "text", recipe: { kind: "copy", source: key } });

Configure a copy from source A as number with wholeNumber=true, then choose source B through the Copy source selector. Its onChange invokes match(field.id, e.target.value), which supplies type=text; the new update branch deletes all numeric policies.

If B contains 1.5 or 'four', recipes.ts skips numeric validation because f.type is now text, leaving an optional destination valid and exportable. This crosses the source-selection/editor boundary into numeric validation and can silently change a saved workflow's business rule.
adversarial|src/ui/MappingRows.tsx|128|c.suggested_fix: Have match preserve the destination's existing output type and compatible field policies when replacing a source reference, instead of always passing type=text. Explicit Output type changes should remain responsible for clearing incompatible settings. Verify remapping a whole-number numeric copy to fractional and nonnumeric sources retains its validation errors.
